todays_decisions.reasoning: I adopt the Market Analyst's risk-off stance at his 0.5 confidence. Bonds, credit, gold and crypto are all falling with stocks, SPY is only 1.42% above its 200-day, 20-day vol is 23.2%, and Nvidia reports tonight. I approve the one proposal, SAM, at its $15 (about 2.4% of equity), and I store it with the Skeptic's three data fixes. I dropped the 11-13 8-K 8.01 clause, which no agent can read (L6: only clauses the inputs can measure). I describe the -0.27 beta as a statistical artifact, not a cushion, as the book already does for KR. I widened the stop to about 10% under the menu close to suit SAM's 0.383 vol (L4: noise should not trip it). On timing I depart in part from my own 11-13 line to deploy after the Nvidia and WMT prints. That line was about broad equity deployment. SAM has no index beta, carries its own stop, has no event until 2027-02-23 (L2: News Analyst date from filings) and is a brewer, not a grocer. It is the kind of name the Market Analyst asks for: small, and in a favored sector. The Skeptic and Implicator are right that it lifts Staples by bucket to about 16.3% before WMT's 11-19 print (L3). That is why it stays at $15 against a $65.77 cap, and why no more Staples goes in before 11-19. Cash ends near $71, about 11.4%. That stays above the 10% buffer on purpose: the stance is risk-off, and per L9 VOO and VTI (about 23.5% of equity together) share one SPY 200-day stop, NEAR at +1.5% per the stop alerts, so one SPY close below 729.58 trips nearly a quarter of the book. I follow the Market Analyst's 'no adds to VOO/VTI before Nvidia' over the owner's invested default. The post-11-19 deployment commitment stands, now also conditional on the regime filter holding. Book review (L7, from the stop blocks): only VOO and VTI are NEAR, every other stop is ok, and none has tripped. EXEL is closest, at 3.2% above $65. VRSN's mark includes a mechanical $0.81 ex-dividend drop today. Qualitative clauses, all untripped: VOO/VTI RSP 21d +2.26% (positive). WMT XLP 21d +5.68% (above +3%), no guidance cut yet, and the 11-16 8-K 5.02 matches the Joe Creed board appointment by inference. That answers the open item, so the conditional WMT reduction I set on 11-16 is not triggered, and no trim was proposed in any case; the close-based $119 stop still does not protect against a gap on the 11-19 print. KR: cyber incident unconfirmed, and Stifel initiated at $80. INCY and EXEL: no new 8-K. DPZ, CARG, IDXX, MSCI, VRSN, FAST: no guidance cut or negative filing. MCO and EXEL: both still on today's 11-17 menu, so their 'screen drops it' clauses can now trip but have not. FAST meets its own 'marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' condition (Industrials on the avoid list); no clause has tripped, so I hold it as the first single stock to cut when cash is needed. L8: the Market Analyst still calls US core the best equity sleeve, so VOO and VTI keep that role. But his 'do not add' contradicts VTI's stored 'the rest can follow after the print', so I restate VTI's thesis. thesis_updates re-date the SPY 200-day to 729.58 for VOO and VTI, give VTI's cost clause a dollar level, and make MCO's text agree with its $470 stop (L6). Note on L3: the exposure packet still files MCO under Industrials by bucket, so Financials is understated; MSCI and MCO together are about 8.3%. No holdings review today.
